truncate

/TRUNG-kayt/ - the stress falls on TRUNG · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Truncate means to shorten by cutting off part of something.

Budget cuts truncated the pier by forty feet, and the pavilion planned for its end was never built.

Example

To fit the shipping crate, the stoneyard sawed a hand's width off the plinth — truncating the base and leaving the statue forever sitting slightly low.

Truncate is more specific than shorten because the loss comes off an end, in one cut — the plinth was not compressed or trimmed all over; its bottom was simply gone.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

shorten: Shorten is the all-purpose word: a thing ends up shorter by any means at all — compressing, thinning, cutting. Truncate is one specific way of shortening: the loss comes off an end, usually in a single blunt cut, and the shape shows it.

clip: Clip means to snip a small, tidy piece off an edge — a coupon, a hedge, a loose thread. Truncate is the heavier act: a whole end lopped off at once, leaving the thing visibly incomplete rather than neatly groomed.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

extend: build the end back out, in space or time

lengthen: make longer overall — the plain opposite

Where it sits · how much of the whole is lost

trim → truncate → gut

trim vs. truncate: Trim is milder — a snip here and there with the shape kept whole; to truncate is to lop the whole end off.

gut vs. truncate: Gut goes further than truncate: not just the tail cut away but the middle hollowed out, until only a shell of the original remains.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — trunc: trunk, lopped stem (Latin truncus)

Suffix — -ate: verb ending: to make or do

Put it together: Trunc (trunk, a lopped stem — Latin truncus) + -ate (verb ending) = to make into a trunk: to cut a thing back the way a felled tree is cut back to its stem. The root stands in plain sight in trunk itself — the main stem left when the branches are gone. Whatever you truncate keeps its base and loses its end.

Use the root in a new word: trunk: The surveyor chalked a blue number on each trunk as she worked down the row.

Root Check

Word Choice

technical / blunt

Truncate is blunt and slightly technical — fields truncate long names, frost truncates seasons, editors truncate columns. The cut always comes off an end, often crudely. If material is squeezed out evenly, condense is honest; if the cuts aim at offense rather than length, that is expurgate, taught in this unit; and cleave, also in this unit, divides a thing into parts rather than shortening it.
